news.title: Data Centers | Calvert County, MD - Official Website

social.text:
10,225 people said: PAUSE DATA CENTERS. And Calvert County listened. 💚

Eight months ago, this started with a petition and a belief that our community deserved time to ask questions, understand the impacts, listen to the science, and have a real voice in decisions that could change Calvert County for generations.

This week, we got that pause.

I was incredibly proud to stand at the rally before the public hearing representing the 10,225 people who added their names to this effort, and even prouder to watch so many people show up and make their voices heard.

Huge thank you to Chesapeake Climate Action Network and Citizens For Calvert for helping organize the rally, and to every person who signed, shared, emailed, called, showed up, spoke up, and kept going.

This was community organizing. And it worked.

Calvert County has a data center moratorium. 💚#CalvertCounty #datacenter #community #rally #SouthernMaryland

quotes.text: This week, we got that pause.

facts: A petition by 10,225 people called for a pause on data centers in Calvert County
Calvert County has a data center moratorium
On Aug. 18, 2026 Calvert County commissioners passed a six-month moratorium on data center site plan approvals (Ordinance 42-26), effective Aug. 28, 2026.
AWS withdrew its Calvert Technology Center application, announced Aug. 4, 2026.
Calvert's updated zoning ordinance took effect March 1, 2025, permitting data centers only in industrial zones I-1 (special exception) and I-2.
Data centers require 200 ft setbacks from property lines and 400 ft from residences.
The most recent Exclusive Negotiating Rights Agreement related to data centers expired May 17, 2026.
